walkthrough:
Relate velocity to acceleration: velocity is the indefinite integral of acceleration with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$

Integrate the linear acceleration $a = 36 - 6t$:
$$v(t) = \int (36 - 6t)\,dt = 36t - \frac{6}{2}t^2 + c = 36t - 3t^2 + c$$

Set the velocity function to zero to find the times of instantaneous rest:
$$-3t^2 + 36t - 33 = 0$$

Divide through by $-3$ to simplify the quadratic:
$$t^2 - 12t + 11 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic expression:
$$(t - 1)(t - 11) = 0$$
$$t = 1\text{ s}\quad \text{and}\quad t = 11\text{ s}$$
